title.en: Ramses and the Pharaoh’s Gold: The Exhibition

ai.en: Ramses and the Pharaohs' Gold is an exhibition at Neon, Battersea Power Station, with 180 treasures lent direct from the Egyptian Museum Cairo. It includes the Coffin of Ramses II, gold masks and silver coffins from Tanis.

events.description: Direct from the Egyptian Museum Cairo. Ramses and the Pharaohs’ Gold brings 180 priceless treasures to London for the first and only time, in an exhibition that explores the extraordinary life, power and legacy of Egypt’s greatest pharaoh. Transporting you from the temples of Abu Simbel to the Valley of the Kings, the exhibition’s crowning masterpiece is the Coffin of Ramses II — a once-in-a-generation opportunity to see the pharaoh’s original sarcophagus. Discover gold masks and silver coffins from the royal tombs of Tanis, beautifully preserved animal mummies and amulets, dazzling jewellery alongside colossal sculptures, carvings and stone heads. Following acclaimed, sold-out runs in Tokyo, Paris, San Francisco and Sydney, Ramses and The Pharaohs’ Gold: The Exhibition runs in London at NEON, Battersea Power Station from 28 February 2026. ABOUT RAMSES Builder, Warrior, God…King Ramses II, widely known as Ramses the Great, ruled Egypt for nearly 67 years and remains history’s most iconic pharaoh. Known for his extensive monument-building, military strategy and diplomacy, and a vast dynasty of more than 100 children, he also negotiated the world’s first recorded peace treaty after the Battle of Kadesh. So powerful was his reign, that the nine pharaohs who followed him all adopted the name of Ramses to emulate his strength and vision. This exhibition invites you to witness the rise of a ruler who sought not only to command an empire, but to secure his immortality for millennia…

title.en: Twist Museum - London's Home of Illusions PEAK

ai.en: Twist Museum in London is an illusion attraction with 80 interactive exhibits. Visitors can see optical illusions, a 3D holographic avatar and shrinking-room effects.

events.description: Welcome to Twist Museum, London’s ultimate illusion experience, where you can discover if you really see colors that don’t exist and explore what you’d look like as a 3D holographic avatar. This immersive playground offers 80 interactive exhibits designed to challenge your mind. See your friends shrink before your eyes, wander through endless corridors, and feel sensations that question your very perception of reality. Step into a world where reality comes with a twist. Grab your tickets now for Twist Museum in London!

Fatherland Pawe Pawlikowski | Poland, Italy, Gremany, France | 2026 | 82m | 12A | In German, French, English and Russian with English subtitles | In Black and White FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family. With FATHERLAND, Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning Ida and Cold War, exploring in his elliptic, distilled style - the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe. Contains suicide references, drug references. Its like a book group but with films Its a Film + Discussion + Coffee evening and everyone is welcome to attend. No membership required. An audience or staff member will give a short introduction, and afterwards you are warmly invited to stay on for an informal post-film discussion over a cuppa. However, there is no obligation to join the discussion; you can leave when the film ends if you would rather.

Part 2 of two films: Résistance and Liberté June 1940. France collapses and signs the armistice. In the midst of the chaos, one man refuses to give up. Alone against the odds, this unknown general flees to London to save what remains of freedom. Without an army, without backing, without hope. But with one irrational conviction - France, his France, has not laid down arms. Taking the ultimate gamble, he seeks to convince the world that the battle for France is neither over, nor lost. Reality, however, is unyielding and seems determined to prove him wrong. Yet, little by little, resistance fighters, rebellious students and determined soldiers rise up in England, France and Africa to join the cause. Their faith, audacity and thirst for freedom defy what history seemed to have written in advance. Language: In French with English subtitiles

title.en: Saturday RnB Lunch | The RnB Collective

ai.en: The R&B Collective hosts a Saturday lunch at Boisdale, Canary Wharf. Lunch reservations start at noon, a DJ plays from noon to 4 pm, and live music runs from 1 to 3 pm.

events.description: Lunch reservations from 12pm | Live music from 1pm to 3pm | DJ from 12pm to 4pm By the time The R&B Collective takes the stage, the room is already warmed up. The DJ starts from midday, lunch is on the table and the soundtrack is pure 90s and 00s R&B. After a run of sold-out evening shows, the five-piece band returns to Boisdale with the songs people still know every word to. Expect smooth vocals, rich harmonies, deep basslines and soulful horn lines, with classics inspired by TLC, Usher, Blackstreet, Donell Jones and Ne-Yo. The set moves from slow jams to singalong hooks and dancefloor favourites, bringing the feel of the era to life without overworking it. It is polished, warm and full of those “I forgot how good this song is” moments. A resident DJ keeps things moving from 12pm to 4pm, with classic R&B and soulful throwbacks before and after the live set. Served alongside Boisdale’s three-course lunch, this is a Saturday made for birthdays, catch-ups, celebrations and groups that want good food with a proper soundtrack. The first-floor bar and outdoor terrace are open for pre-show and post-show drinks until late, subject to availability. 'Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski Everest’s direct North Face - the most dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on earth. Thousands have summited via Nepal’s southeast ridge, but only a handful have reached the top by this route, and no one has ever skied down. From the duo that brought us Touching the Void Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin latest cinematic journey explores love, loss and courage. Seven years in the making, the film required documenting a near-impossible expedition in one of the most remote places on Earth. '

events.description: Brunch from 12:00pm | Last Reservation 3:00pm | Music 12:30-3:30pm The Saturday Brunch Club runs every weekend on the first floor, and the format is straightforward: a two-course brunch, a Boisdale Bellini on arrival and a DJ from the Boisdale live music roster in the booth. The terrace overlooks Cabot Square and the fountain, it is heated and there is no timer on the afternoon. The DJ rotates weekly, which means the music shifts depending on who is playing. Live instrumental elements come in across the set. Add free-flowing wine if the occasion calls for it. Two-course brunch with a complimentary Boisdale Bellini – £39.50 Add free-flowing red, white or sparkling wine – £25 per person First Floor Bar & Heated Garden Terrace Nestled in Cabot Square and overlooking the fountain with the Canary Wharf skyline beyond, the first floor bar and heated garden terrace is a destination in its own right. Fine wines, premium spirits and expertly crafted cocktails, with a selection that covers everything from rare whiskies to classic and signature serves. Pair your drink with Scottish cuisine, fresh seafood, steaks, burgers, pizzas and more. The bar hosts DJ nights Thursday through Saturday and brunch on the terrace every Saturday and Sunday. events.description: 12 stops across London, roughly 63 minutes of narration, walked in whatever order and at whatever speed suits you. Works fully offline once downloaded, so you need no data or signal while you walk. Your code never expires and there is no fixed date - buy now and use it whenever you next visit. Explore London at your own pace A lion's paw once struck fear from its perch in Trafalgar Square and secret oaths echoed within the marble halls of the Reform Club. Westminster is layered with more intrigue than meets the eye-each stone concealing lost rebellions and whispered betrayals. Turn your city walk into a self-guided audio adventure, revealing iconic landmarks and backstreet secrets alike. Glide past history's grand stage and dive into stories that most passersby never hear. Who plotted treason beneath the stern gaze of Admiral Nelson? What masterpiece at the National Gallery inspired a scandal that rocked Victorian society? And whose footprints still mark a midnight escape through the columns of the Reform Club? 'Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski Everest’s direct North Face - the most dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on earth. Thousands have summited via Nepal’s southeast ridge, but only a handful have reached the top by this route, and no one has ever skied down. From the duo that brought us Touching the Void Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin latest cinematic journey explores love, loss and courage. Seven years in the making, the film required documenting a near-impossible expedition in one of the most remote places on Earth. '

Can you put a price on happiness, beauty and love? A brand new world-premiere play from the Olivier Award-winning playwright, James Graham (Punch, Dear England, Labour of Love) explodes into the West End for a strictly limited 12-week run. Directed by multi award-winner Nicholas Hytner (The History Boys, One Man, Two Guvnors, Giant) and starring Olivier Award winner Rory Kinnear (Skyfall, The Diplomat) and Royal Ballet principal Natalia Osipova in her West End debut, this blazing new play tells the astonishing story of rebel economist and member of the Bloomsbury Group, John Maynard Keynes. Husband to ballerina Lydia Lopokova. Lover to Duncan Grant. Friend to Virginia Woolf. Keynes moves between the corridors of power in Whitehall and the intoxicating freedom of a radical circle of artists, writers and lovers - all determined to live differently. But as markets crash, old systems crumble and Britain teeters on the edge of chaos, one question begins to consume him: What is a good life? Alive with music, dance, desire and debate, The Standard of Living is a thrilling, funny and deeply moving portrait of a man who dared to imagine something better. Opening at the Theatre Royal Haymarket from 21 September for a strictly limited 12-week season.

Thirty years after it redefined musical theatre, Jonathan Larson's groundbreaking musical RENT bursts back onto the West End in a bold new production directed by Luke Sheppard (& Juliet, Paddington The Musical) and starring Gaten Matarazzo (Stranger Things) as Mark. Set in New York's East Village, RENT follows a group of young artists, musicians and friends, navigating love, ambition and creativity while trying to build lives on their own terms. Inspired by Puccini's La Bohème, this iconic musical captures the joy, uncertainty and resilience of a generation determined to make every moment count. Featuring an unforgettable score and a story that continues to resonate, RENT is a powerful celebration of community, connection and a call to live every minute as if it were your last. Kristin Scott Thomas returns to the West End in a gripping new production of THE CHERRY ORCHARD,Anton Chekhov’s poignant and piercing tragicomedy about a family on the brink of irreversiblechange. Olivier and Tony Award nominated Director Ian Rickson (Uncle Vanya, Jerusalem, The Weir), reunites with Olivier Award winner Conor McPherson (Uncle Vanya, Girl from the North Country, The Weir) for a new adaptation produced by Sonia Friedman Productions (Oedipus, Leopoldstadt, Jerusalem) Chekhov’s final masterpiece captures a world in delicate, inevitable transition – and remains as timeless and resonant as ever. “Without the cherry orchard, life has no meaning to me” When Lyubov Ranevskaya (Kristin Scott Thomas) returns to her childhood estate after years abroad, she finds her family home and beloved cherry orchard under threat. As old loyalties falter and new ambitions rise, a world of privilege begins to crumble. Can Lyubov embrace the future, or will the pull of memory prove impossible to escape? Don’t miss this deeply moving portrait of love, loss and letting go...Opening at the Harold Pinter Theatre for a strictly limited season from 3 October 2026 until 9 January 2027. AUDIO DESCRIBED: Saturday, 31st October 2026, 2:30pm, Saturday, 14th November 2026, 2:30pm BSL SIGNED: Saturday, 7th November 2026, 2:30pm

Emmy, two-time Tony, Screen Actors Guild and Drama Desk winner Christine Baranski makes her West End debut as the iconic Judith Bliss, sparring with Academy Award nominated stage and screen legend Richard E. Grant in a stinging new production of Noël Coward’s irresistible comedy directed by Emily Burns. Last year, Judith retired from her life-on-stage. Already, she misses the applause. Idling away at their country home, the rest of the family – reclusive novelist husband David and failure-to-launch children Sorrel and Simon – are too self-involved to be a good audience. So, Judith invites a young fan as her guest for the weekend. But unbeknownst to her, each of the Blisses have a guest of their own arriving at the very same time. Completely unsuited to hosting and allergic to compromise, the house quickly erupts into a chaos of parlour games, put-downs and unrequested encores. events.description: Florian Henckel von Donnersmarcks The Lives of Others at the Adelphi Theatre is set in 1984 East Germany, where a writer and an actor are placed under state surveillance. From the attic above their apartment, a Stasi officer listens for evidence of subversion, as the story examines what happens when observation starts to change the observer.

On the night of December 4, 1956, four musical icons walked into a recording studio in Memphis and made musical history. Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis, Carl Perkins and Elvis Presley were brought together by pure chance for a jam session which would go on to shape the trajectory of rock 'n' roll music globally. Featuring the hit songs Blue Suede Shoes, Fever, Walk The Line, Hound Dog, Great Balls of Fire, and many more, experience that once-in-a-lifetime event, in an electrifying 3x Tony Award-nominated musical where rivalries ignited, friendships were tested and rock 'n' roll was born. Starring stage and screen favourite, Darren Day (Hollyoaks, Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, Chicago) as Sam Phillips, the visionary producer who discovered the sound of rock 'n' roll, alongside a sensational cast and live band, don't miss this exhilarating celebration of legendary artists.

HADESTOWN, the acclaimed Broadway musical phenomenon by singer-songwriter Anais Mitchell and director Rachel Chavkin makes its long-awaited West End premiere in February 2024 at the Lyric Theatre. ‘An epic celebration of music, togetherness and hope’ (Forbes). HADESTOWN is the winner of 8 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the Grammy Award® for Best Musical Theatre Album. HADESTOWN takes you on an unforgettable journey to the underworld and back, intertwining two mythic love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone. A deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience, HADESTOWN invites you to imagine how the world could be. ‘Your next musical theatre obsession’ (Vogue). ‘Sumptuous. Gorgeous. As good as it gets’ (New York Times) ‘A transporting musical hit! Anaïs Mitchell’s score is a joyful combination of folk, pop, Dixieland and blues. You’ll be singing it in your head for days’ (Time Out)

Following a sold-out UK & Ireland tour, multi-award-winning master showman Derren Brown brings his extraordinary new live show Only Human to the West End. In this brand-new production, Derren Brown combines mind-reading, psychological illusion, and breathtaking storytelling in a way that is both deeply personal and utterly electrifying. Only Human explores what it means to be human - our perceptions, our beliefs, and the fragile line between reality and illusion. Smart, unsettling, and wildly entertaining, this is theatre at its most compelling. Some experiences stay with you. This one could change you. Prepare to have your mind blown! A haunting musical inspired by Georg Büchner's Woyzeck. Franz & Marie is a unique and visceral musical that breathes new life into Georg Büchner’s classic German tragedy, Woyzeck, with soul-rattling Indie Raw Folk. It was originally commissioned two decades ago by the award-winning Korean company Acom and created by key members of the Kentish underground cult band, The Singing Loins. This musical transforms a legendary tale into a heart-breaking tragedy, that explores contemporary themes of class prejudice and toxic masculinity, infused with sharp dark humour. Franz & Marie is a visceral, journey into the heart of a good man broken by a bad world.Set in the twisted world of late 19th Century European Folklore, after action on the front line a platoon of young soldiers has been stationed in an isolated outpost for months awaiting further orders. Among them is Franz Woyzeck, a man haunted by nightmares since his return. He sees fire in the sky—hallucinations that blur the line between reality and trauma. Franz lives for two people: his girlfriend Marie, and their baby, Georgie. Forbidden from taking leave during the war, they haven’t been able to marry, but his devotion is absolute- he goes above and beyond to provide for Marie and his child. The title Franz & Marie refers to Woyzeck’s first name and that of his girlfriend. Much like Romeo and Juliet, they love each other deeply and set out on an unforgiving path that could lead them to a bitter, tragic end. In this musical…

Featuring powerhouse voices and show-stopping numbers such as My Heart Will Go On, All by Myself and To Love You More – backed by a full live band – TITANIQUE is a one-of-a-kind theatrical voyage bursting with nostalgia, heart and campy chaos. See you aboard the Ship of Dreams, girlfriends!

Agatha Christie’s The Mousetrap is the world’s longest-running play. This thrilling West End production is the genre-defining murder mystery from the best-selling novelist of all time… case closed! As news spreads of a murder in London, a group of seven strangers find themselves snowed in at a remote countryside guesthouse. When a police sergeant arrives, the guests discover – to their horror – that a killer is in their midst! Which one is the murderer? Who will be their next victim? Can you solve this world-famous mystery for yourself? For almost 70 years, Agatha Christie’s The Mousetrap has kept millions of people from every corner of the globe on the edge of their seats.

Fatherland Pawe Pawlikowski | Poland, Italy, Gremany, France | 2026 | 82m | 12A | In German, French, English and Russian with English subtitles | In Black and White FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family. With FATHERLAND, Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning Ida and Cold War, exploring in his elliptic, distilled style - the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe. This captivating programme, performed by the celebrated Piccadilly Sinfonietta and leading violinist to be announced, promises an evening of elegance and inspiration. events.description: AEG Presents Cancer Bats For more than 20 years, Canadian hardcore heavyweights Cancer Bats have delivered uncompromising intensity. They’ve toured the globe relentlessly, released seven acclaimed studio albums — six of which earned JUNO nominations — and built a legacy on raw, sweat-soaked, unforgettable live performances. Over the course of their career, Cancer Bats have cultivated a devoted, almost cult-like global following. Their success spans multiple continents, from Australia to Europe, with performances across Japan, China, and Nepal. The United Kingdom, in particular, has become a stronghold for the band, rivaling their success in Canada. Years of relentless touring, coverage in publications such as Kerrang! and Metal Hammer, regular airplay across BBC Radio, and appearances at major festivals including Download, Leeds & Reading, Slam Dunk, and 2000 Trees have all helped cement their position. Two decades in and thousands of shows deep, Cancer Bats have honed their craft to a masterful level — and they’re nowhere near slowing down. The group based their name on “Pieces of Dreams,” a cover tune by Stanley Turrentine that the group performed. events.description: ✨ Welcome to the fantastical worlds of Tim Burton! We invite you to celebrate this Halloween weekend on a journey through the music that made it unforgettable. At the heart of it all is the music of Danny Elfman, Burton’s lifelong collaborator and one of the most distinctive film composers of our time. Elfman’s music blends playfulness with menace, tenderness with grandeur — a perfect mirror of Burton’s visual imagination. Alongside Elfman, highlights include unforgettable moments from Corpse Bride, the cult favourite Beetlejuice, the gothic sweep of Batman, and the razor-sharp drama of Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street. events.description: Dinner & Table Reservations from 5pm. DJs from 8pm-2am Saxon Sound System started in Lewisham in 1976 and spent the next fifty years becoming one of the most significant forces in British music, which is not an overstatement. They pioneered the fast-chat MC style that gave birth to jungle, drum and bass, UK garage and grime. They launched Maxi Priest, Tippa Irie, Smiley Culture and Papa Levi. In 1988 they went to Jamaica and defeated opponents on their home turf, something no UK sound had done before. In 1992 they won the UK Cup Clash. In 1994 they became the first UK sound system to win the World Clash. Jazzie B credits them as a key influence on Soul II Soul. Massive Attack invited them to curate the 2008 Meltdown festival. Chuck D, KRS-One and Wycliffe Jean were all stopped in their tracks by Saxon cassette tapes. David Rodigan has been saluting them for decades. On Saturday nights at Boisdale, Musclehead, Sean M, Victor V and Sir Allan Brando bring that history to the first floor bar. The format is exactly what Saxon has always done best: the latest and the classic, mixed live with MCs on the mic and shout-outs bookable on the night for anyone celebrating. This is not a tribute to what Saxon used to be. It is Saxon, still doing it. Fatherland Pawe Pawlikowski | Poland, Italy, Gremany, France | 2026 | 82m | 12A | In German, French, English and Russian with English subtitles | In Black and White FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family. With FATHERLAND, Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning Ida and Cold War, exploring in his elliptic, distilled style - the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe. ai.en: Tom Rush, the folk singer famed for No Regrets, plays Union Chapel. It is his first London concert since the 1960s.

events.description: AGMP Presents AGMP Concerts proudly presents TOM RUSH Folk legend famed for 'No Regrets' announces his first London concert since the 1960's. Tom Rush helped shape the folk revival in the '60s and the renaissance of the '80s and '90s, his music having left its stamp on generations of artists. James Taylor told Rolling Stone, "Tom was not only one of my early heroes, but also one of my main influences." Country music star Garth Brooks has credited Rush with being one of his top five musical influences. Tom Rush began his musical career in the early '60s playing the Boston-area clubs while a Harvard student. He had released two albums 'Tom Rush at the Unicorn' and 'Got A Mind To Ramble' by the time he graduated. In 1967, Tom Rush released his signature song 'No Regrets' which went on to be covered by The Walker Brothers, Midge Ure, Emmylou Harris, Shirley Bassey, Waylon Jennings, Curtis Stigers and many more. Tom Rush has long championed emerging artists. His early recordings introduced the world to the work of Joni Mitchell, Jackson Browne and James Taylor, and in more recent years his Club 47(R) concerts have brought artists such as Nanci Griffith and Shawn Colvin to wider audiences when they were just beginning to build their own reputations. Don't miss your chance to see Tom Rush live and direct from the USA at the Union Chapel on the 1st November 2026.
Plus support from Bramwell and Godzooki

Trumpeter/composer Kenny Warren grew up in Denver and has lived in NYC since 2006. He has made over a dozen records as a bandleader and solo artist, has performed all over the world, and was recognized by Downbeat Magazine as a Raising Star in 2025 and 2026. In 2024 his trio Sweet World with cellist Christopher Hoffman and drummer Nathan Ellman-Bell released an LP on Out of Your Head Records which the Best of Bandcamp hailed as “the sonic representation of a beating heart”. Sweet World has a follow up record due in 2027. He has also made 3 LPs with his avant-country outfit Laila and Smitty, two jazz records for the London based Whirlwind Recordings, and a series of covid-era solo records which are available exclusively on bandcamp. Warren's 20 plus years in Brooklyn have produced a body of work in conversation with generations of the city's greatest musical artists. Current NY based collaborations include work with the original-song-driven band Slow Tiger, an improvised collective with Carlo Costa & BlankFor.ms, and a duo with Gregg Belisle-Chi. Warren is also a frequent collaborator with the Berlin based artist, Jeremy Viner, and the Denver based band Mountain Coast. events.description: Stan Rennie & his family have worked the same stretch of coastline, where the river meets the sea for centuries. Dealing with the devastation of his business and his own failing health, Stan finds himself thrown into a battle for the future. As officials equivocate, he becomes the unlikely figurehead for a grassroots campaign to uncover the truth about the die-off, managing it in the only way he knows how, with heart, determination and a rich strain of gallows humour. A wry, David and Goliath story about navigating through grief and finding power in community. New installation by Spanish artist Cristina Reyes La Sombra Azul is a site-responsive installation that transforms the gallery into a quiet sanctuary amid London’s movement. Operating between two and three dimensions, this hybrid mural- sculpture acts as a playful totem bridging realms as an urban guardian. The work explores our ancient impulse to express what rational language cannot through symbolic figures. Painted live in a performative ritual where the artist temporarily merges with the space, the installation brings an active protective presence into being rather than a static object. As the debut project in Reyes’s Guardianes series, it offers a moment of pause and curiosity, reimagining ritual and myth within modern urban life. The work will be produced in the gallery from 1 to 11 November, with the artist creating the work live and incorporating her own body into the process, as if she were part of the artwork itself. The work becomes a performance and the performance becomes part of the work, bringing the guardian to life through action.

events.description: Tortoise is widely considered one of the most influential music groups of the last 40 years, with a wide-reaching impact on the contemporary music scene. Pitchfork says: “Imagine a graphic showing all the bands the five members of Tortoise were in before they came together and then all the bands they went on to play with after. At the top of the funnel you have groups ranging from dreamy psych-rock to earthy post-punk crunch, including Eleventh Dream Day, Bastro, Slint, and the Poster Children; on the 'post-Tortoise' end are groups focusing on electro-jazz and twangy instrumental rock like Isotope 217, Chicago Underground, and Brokeback. In this graphic, Tortoise is the choke point, the one project that has elements of all these sounds but is never defined by nor committed to any of them. Instead, Tortoise floats free, a planchette moving over a Ouija board guided by 10 sets of fingers, where everyone watches the arrow float in one direction but no one is quite sure how it gets there or who is doing the pushing.”. Initially hailed as pace-setters of the then-emerging, so-called “post-rock” sound (a wording band never have really been happy with), the Chicago Tribune called Tortoise’s sound “mood music that refuses to be shoved into the background, as inviting as it is challenging.” Releasing just seven albums since 1990 — including classics like 1996’s Millions Now Living Will Never Die, 1998’s TNT, and 2001’s Standards —Tortoise has steadily and intuitively evolved across…

events.description: ICA presents the UK premiere of a collaborative project between celebrated LA producer/DJ Nosaj Thing and Daito Manabe, Tokyo's godfather of audio-visual innovation. Support is a live set from Tristan Arp. As DJ and producer Nosaj Thing has been actively releasing music and performing for 15 years, producing tracks for Kendrick Lamar, Kid Cudi, and Chance The Rapper, and remixing a diverse roster of generation-spanning artists including Philip Glass, Charlotte Gainsbourg and Flying Lotus. The impressive and long-standing cultural dialogue between the ever-evolving two artists started with the agenda-setting 2012 music video for 'Eclipse/Blue' featuring Kazu Makino of Blonde Redhead, through to the boundary breaking 'No Reality' global tour that was unveiled at Coachella 2016 - through to the recently improvised showcase at FIL. Entitled 'Material Works', the 2026 performance series was launched as a live AV installation, Nosaj and Daito joined by designer David Rudnick. Their new single 'LXR' introduces a new era for the storied partnership, one that follows their acclaimed collaborative live performance at Future Frequencies Festival in Tokyo at MoN Takanawa: The Museum of Narratives, and the release of Daito Manabe's debut EP 'dm studies 00 - 004' on Nosaj Thing's Timetable. events.description: Doors 7:45 PM, Music 8:30 PM - 2 set(s) of music Line-up: Rebecka Edlund - Voice Laura Jurd - Trumpet Ruth Goller - Bass guitar About Swedish vocalist Rebecka Edlund weaves together the sonorities of experimental jazz and Scandinavian folk music. Since moving from Sweden to London in 2019, Edlund has established herself as one of the UK’s boldest pioneers within vocal improvisation and songwriting. Drawing on the evocative edge of Nordic landscapes and the quirks of human nature, Edlund’s music is defined by immersive storytelling, expressive improvisations, herding calls and bird whistles. Join comedian and host Tommy Sandhu and Bollywood vocalist Chirag Rao for a unique evening where no two shows are ever the same. Forget the traditional concert. Mehfil Masti is an intimate night of music, comedy and audience interaction where you help steer the show and create the playlist. Tommy’s quick wit and infectious banter keep the laughs coming while Chirag performs Bollywood classics from the 60s through to the 00s, including timeless favourites, romantic hits and feel good anthems, accompanied by high quality backing tracks. Whether it is a song that reminds you of your childhood, your wedding, your first love or simply your favourite Bollywood hero, put in your request and Chirag may perform it live on the night. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. He must confront what he's willing to sacrifice, who he's willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side. Brought to life with a live string quartet and filmed live from the Almeida Theatre, Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (Vanya) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success.

ai.en: Dabeull, a French producer and artist who is a leading figure in the global funk revival, plays Troxy.

events.description: Dabeull is a visionary French producer and artist, widely regarded as a leading figure in the global funk revival. With his unmistakable blend of punchy basslines, retro synthesizers, and sensual vocals, he has carved out an unique place on the international music scene. Known for his 70s?80s movie star aesthetic and analog obsession, Dabeull channels the golden era of funk with unmatched authenticity. His sound is deeply influenced by the Pop, Funk and African Music he was exposed to during his youth, infused with the warmth of vintage gear and recorded entirely using classic 70s synthesizers. Whether in the studio or on stage, Dabeull is a master of groove. His live shows?featuring a full analog band, period costumes, and retro instrumentation?transport audiences on a nostalgic, feel-good journey through funk history.With a growing global fanbase and a distinct artistic identity, Dabeull continues to redefine modern funk while honoring its timeless roots.

Three men, three eras and one hidden connection shape this boldly cinematic Spanish drama about love, secrets and the weight of the past. Shifting between 1932, 1937 and 2017 with ease, at first these three stories seem completely separate, but gradually connections emerge between the men at their centre. Desire, buried family truths and a forgotten piece of history bind their lives across generations, with an unfinished work of Federico García Lorca hanging over the whole story. From its virtuoso opening scene, this sweeping epic announces itself as an assured piece of filmmaking. Stunning location work, breathtaking composition and meticulous period detail create a richly textured world where personal and national histories collide. Look out for supporting turns from Glenn Close and a heavily award-tipped Penélope Cruz.

title.en: Iphigenie en Tauride - English National Opera

events.description: Iphigénie and her brother Oreste are the children of the most blood-soaked dynasty in Greek history. Their inheritance is a legacy of violence dating back to the dawn of time. Her journey has taken her to a forlorn temple at the ends of the earth. His has taken him to the edge of madness. Each fears the other is dead. Stranded on a remote island, forced to minister to the wishes of a terrifying ruler, Iphigenie dreams of home. The hope that she will one day reunite with her brother Oreste is all that stands between her and despair. So, when a mysterious stranger washes up on the island’s shores with news of the collapse of her family, Iphigenie fears the worst. But is all as hopeless as first seems? Or is there more to this stranger than meets the eye? Find out what fate has in store for the siblings, in a new interpretation of this rarely performed operatic masterpiece.

Three men, three eras and one hidden connection shape this boldly cinematic Spanish drama about love, secrets and the weight of the past. Shifting between 1932, 1937 and 2017 with ease, at first these three stories seem completely separate, but gradually connections emerge between the men at their centre. Desire, buried family truths and a forgotten piece of history bind their lives across generations, with an unfinished work of Federico García Lorca hanging over the whole story. From its virtuoso opening scene, this sweeping epic announces itself as an assured piece of filmmaking. Stunning location work, breathtaking composition and meticulous period detail create a richly textured world where personal and national histories collide. Look out for supporting turns from Glenn Close and a heavily award-tipped Penélope Cruz.

Led by Zambia-born, London-raised singer-songwriter Hilary Mwelwa, this is soul with roots in Aretha Franklin, Stevie Wonder and Marvin Gaye, but shaped by London R&B, jazz-soul and the smooth US soul sound that embraced her early. She went on to appear on Later... with Jools Holland, share stages with James Brown, D’Angelo and Macy Gray, and find US radio success with her version of "For the Love of You". The live set draws from a catalogue that includes "Until You Come Back to Me", "For the Love of You", "Pieces", "Strictly a Vibe Thing" and newer material from Back in Love and Nasalifya (Thank You). Expect warm keys, a rhythm section that sits in the pocket, close backing vocals and Hilary’s lead vocal right where it should be: relaxed, soulful and never overworked. At Boisdale of Canary Wharf, this is a strong fit for the room: grown-up UK soul, neo-soul detail, jazz-soul colour and songs that reward close listening as much as they reward a good groove. events.description: DAY FEVER HAS TAKEN OVER THE COUNTRY! The day-time clubbing event started by Vicky McClure, Jonny Owen and Reverend & The Makers has swept the UK since it’s launch in 2024 ‘The day-time disco that doesn’t ruin your Sunday’ has amassed a huge following with thousands of punters packing out clubs and theatres every weekend to dance the day away from. A whole generation who perhaps thought their clubbing days were behind them are blazing a trail for a new way to enjoy themselves. Day Fever prides itself on creating a safe-space where people can just be themselves. No dress code, no egos, just enjoyment and positivity. This has seen a loyal fanbase leading to sold out shows in some of the countries most famous venues. The music policy is simple, the greatest hits of the 20th century. Why can’t Madonna sit next to Madness? Pulp go back to back with Prince? The Stone Roses and The Rolling Stones? 90’s dance classics versus a spot of Motown? Why choose when you can enjoy it all? events.description: DHP Presents KÄÄRIJÄ EURODISKO - TOUR 2026 Plus Special Guest Little Sis Nora After launching the biggest show of his career at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki next spring - a show that is already almost sold out - Käärijä will continue his major concert year by conquering Europe with his most extensive European tour yet in autumn 2026. The EURODISKO TOUR 2026 will feature a massive 24 shows in 16 different countries across Europe. Käärijä has been performing tailored gigs this past year in Europe and Asia, and fans have been eagerly waiting for a new tour abroad. Käärijä has already been on two European tours previously in his career, in 2023 and 2024. The majority of Käärijä’s previous tours’ shows sold out in just minutes, and venues had to be upgraded to larger ones. Having risen to become an unprecedented international phenomenon, Käärijä has been awarded with five Finnish Grammy Awards as well as the Best Nordic Artist award at the MTV EMA awards. title.en: Mark Thomas: 40 in Stand Up Years

events.description: What?! Mark Thomas has been ‘standing up’ for 40 years? Impossible!! But how old does that make you…? Alas it is true; one of our oldest surviving alternative comics celebrates 40 years at the mic as he takes his brand-new show on the road this autumn. So, here’s what he has done so far in numbers; performed comedy for 40 years, won 8 awards for performing, 4 for human rights work and 1 he invented for himself, made 6 series of the Mark Thomas Comedy Product (Channel 4), written 6 books and 5 play scripts, made 5 series of the Manifesto for Radio 4, made 3 Dispatches for Channel 4, sued the police (and won) 3 times, curated and authored 2 art exhibitions with artist Tracey Moberly and had 1 Guinness World Record for holding 20 protests in 24 hours. If that’s not enough, he’s also walked 724km around the length of the Israel Wall in the West Bank, been credited with changing the law on tax avoidance, started a comedy club in Palestine with Dr Sam Beale and campaigned successfully for things like trade union recognition for cinema workers and getting multinationals to change their practices. You’re right, there’s more, but your attention is running out and we’re running out of space. So, let’s just say he’s generally mucked about trying to have fun and upset the right people…which he is really, really good at. This is a taster menu of political and personal mayhem, jokes, rants and a state of the nation broadcast as he tries to turn ‘what the hell is going on’ into a cogent…

As well as her solo project she is also part of the groups Irreversible Entanglements and 700 Bliss. Support from Peruvian harpist Eva Matin. Fetish bones 10th anniversary First released September 16, 2016, Fetish Bones was the debut album of Philadelphia based musician, artist, and activist Camae Ayewa, performing as Moor Mother. Recorded in her home studio using a collection of machines, field recordings, and analog noisemakers, the album's 13 tracks fused the visceral anger of punk with the expansive improvisatory spirit of Sun Ra, arriving not as a way to forget but as a demand to remember. The record was named an Album of the Year by The Wire and Jazz Right Now, and landed on Pitchfork's Best Experimental LPs of 2016, Rolling Stone's Best Avant Albums of 2016, and Thump's 25 Best Experimental Albums of 2016. 'Deadbeat Protest' made both Pitchfork's and Noisey's Best Songs of 2016 lists, and Bandcamp named Ayewa its 2016 Artist of the Year while including Fetish Bones among its 100 Best Records of 2016. Ten years later, Don Giovanni Records celebrates that debut with a 10th anniversary edition, pressed with a foil album cover and featuring the previously unreleased bonus track 'Marian Anderson,' a collaboration with Wolf Weston and Wooden Elephant. title.en: Flea Circus: the Smallest Show on Earth. A Talk by Dr Tim Cockerill

events.description: Roll up and see the world-famous performing fleas! For over 150 years, audiences have been paying their sixpences to be amazed by whole troupes of real, live, performing fleas. Believe it, or not? In this talk Tim will persuade you that the flea circus, until recently, was a 100% genuine spectacle, made up of live fleas pulling chariots, riding tricycles and even fighting duels with perfectly crafted miniature swords. Find out how the Flea Circus 'Professors' fed their fleas, which household appliance spelled the demise of the Flea Circus in the 1950s, and how a flea could make a Victorian lady take all of her clothes off. Features rare images and footage from Tim's Flea Circus collection. About Dr Tim Cockerill Tim specialises in documenting and communicating the spectacular diversity of life on earth. He has a PhD in tropical ecology from the University of Cambridge and is a Fellow of the Royal Entomological Society. Tim has explored some of the most biodiverse places on the planet, from the rainforests of Papua New Guinea to the spiny forests of Madagascar. On TV Tim is a presenter, contributor and consultant. He has wrangled rhinoceros beetles and flying lizards in Borneo with Sir David Attenborough and has presented Britain's only genuine flea circus on the Royal Institution Christmas Lectures. Tim has talked about spiders live on The One Show and about eels and leeches live on CBBC. On radio Tim has been the resident zoologist on BBC Radio 4's Inside Science and on…

events.description: This year’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner stars two 2025 Oscar nominees - Renate Reinsve (Sentimental Value) and Sebastian Stan (The Apprentice) - in a gripping, morally complex drama that will leave you thinking about it long after the credits roll. A Romanian-Norwegian family moves to a small village at the end of a beautiful fjord. They quickly befriend their neighbours and their children settle into school. But when bruises are discovered on their daughter, rumours begin to spread. Is something wrong at home, or are they simply raising their children differently from everyone else? Winning his second Palme d’Or after 2007’s 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, Romanian director Cristian Mungiu turns a seemingly peaceful village into the setting for a tense, unsettling moral drama that refuses easy answers. Sebastian Stan gives an impressively restrained performance as the father, while Renate Reinsve is a calm, disquieting presence as his Norwegian wife. Slowly and surely, Fjord transforms an everyday community dispute into something far more disturbing.

events.description: Table reservations from 6pm | Live Music: 8.30pm “Each performer is a master of his craft...”London’s Magic FM The Definitive Rat Pack returns to Boisdale with Stephen Triffitt as Frank Sinatra, Mark Adams as Dean Martin and Darren Charles as Sammy Davis Jr, joined by Hannah Lindsey as Nancy Sinatra. This is the Rat Pack done by performers who have lived with the material for years, not a loose swing set in dinner jackets. Triffitt and Adams starred in the West End’s The Rat Pack: Live from Las Vegas, and Darren Charles brings the Sammy Davis Jr sharpness: rhythm, pace, humour and that switch from charm to attack when the song needs it. Hannah Lindsey adds the Nancy Sinatra edge, taking the night from classic Vegas swing into 60s pop cool with "Bang Bang", "These Boots Are Made for Walkin’" and "Somethin’ Stupid". That contrast matters: Sinatra’s late-night phrasing, Dean’s relaxed swing, Sammy’s snap and Nancy’s cool, clipped delivery all sit in different corners of the same room. Expect "Fly Me to the Moon", "That’s Amore", "Mr Bojangles", "Bang Bang" and "Somethin’ Stupid", with a live band keeping the pace tight and the arrangements properly dressed. Boisdale of Canary Wharf gives it the right setting: dinner, cocktails, whisky and a stage close enough for the jokes, the timing and the good notes to land. events.description: Event Calendar CLICK HERE After four years of events, Co:See Chats arrives at Soul Mama this November for a live show filled with laughter, unapologetic conversation, and a celebration of Black cinema. Co:See Chats is a live show for us, by us, and about us and the lives we’re actually living, inspired by the films that raised us. From classic movies to new features, we screen clips from iconic cinema to spark honest and unapologetic real talk about love, life and culture. We’re here to connect with each other, laugh at ourselves, and leave a little lighter than we came in. The conversation is guided by a panel of our favourite commentators; audience members can share their perspectives and challenge the panel and each other live! You can grab the microphone or sit back and enjoy the conversation: either way, we invite you to share the view. Whether it is discussing Roland’s betrayal of Lance in “The Best Man”, Helen’s revenge on Charles in “Diary of a Mad Black Woman”, or Shanté mind games in “Two Can Play That Game”, we explore the characters and choices in the films we love, and reflect on these and our relationships with others. After all: they do say films are windows and mirrors! For a mid-week experience guaranteed to make you laugh and discuss long after the event ends, join us at Co:See Chats. Check out our socials for more information @cosee_chats The Soul Mama Menu offers a delightful blend of African, Caribbean, and South American cuisine. Soul Mama was listed in…

Horse Lords co-presented by ICA and Baba Yaga's Hut. Support from Damian Dalla Torre. Horse Lords were founded in Baltimore in 2010; they evolved from the experimental collective Teeth Mountain and began as a trio with drummer Sam Haberman, guitarist Owen Gardner, and bassist Max Eilbacher, soon adding alto saxophonist Andrew Bernstein to the core ensemble. Though Horse Lords grew out of the fertile Baltimore noise and leftfield rock scene, a storied environment for artists and weirdos that has nurtured many an influential outsider band (Lungfish, Matmos), their approach is more omnivorous than the stippled rhythms of instrumental electric rock would indicate. Across sixteen years of frequent touring, Horse Lords have released ten studio, live, and collaboration albums in addition to a split EP with fellow Baltimoreans Lower Dens, a handful of singles and compilation tracks. For RVNG’s FRKWYS series, the band collaborated with Berlin-based composer Arnold Dreyblatt, a onetime student of La Monte Young and Pauline Oliveros whose just intonation chamber music was a crucial part of the post-Fluxus Downtown New York City environment. Presented by Institute of Contemporary Arts. This is an 18+ event

ai.en: Bleak Squad, a Melbourne art-rock band, plays The Victoria. The band includes Mick Turner of Dirty Three and Mick Harvey of Nick Cave and The Bad Seeds.

events.description: Bleak Squad is a new Melbourne four-piece comprised of true Australian art-rock royalty. Featuring Mick Turner (Dirty Three, Mess Esque) Mick Harvey (Nick Cave &The Bad Seeds, PJ Harvey, The Birthday Party), Adalita (Magic Dirt) and Marty Brown (Art of Fighting), the unlikely quartet unite for the first time on Bleak Squad’s brooding, noir-rock debut LP, Strange Love, since shortlisted for the Australian Music Prize. Borne from spur of the moment jam sessions, Strange Love sees all four members juggle multiple instruments, songwriting, their own idiosyncrasies, and lead vocal duties between Adalita and Harvey. The result is a confident nine-song set of love, loss and lonesome-ness, set to fizzing guitars, slippery bass lines, and the signature illogical squawk of Turner’s guitar. With Strange Love, Bleak Squad announce the boldest of entries into the Australian music landscape. “…they should not be missed live: four Australian music greats with charisma to burn, uncanny chemistry, and a quality set of songs tailor-made for those long, dark nights of the soul.” Andrew Stafford, The Guardian Plus support from Jess Ribeiro

ai.en: Family Band plays Vortex Jazz Club. Doors open at 7:45 pm, and music starts at 8:30 pm, across two sets.

events.description: Doors 7:45 PM, Music 8:30 PM – 2 sets of music Line-up: Kim Macari – Trumpet Riley Stone-Lonergan – Tenor saxophone Tom Rivière – Double bass Steve Hanley – Drum kit About: Comprising four long-term collaborators and friends (thus the ‘family’ tag), the band takes as its starting point the freewheeling music of those musicians who, back in the 1960s, were at the forefront of the free jazz revolution, but whose opening up of jazz’s constraints is now recognised as not a break from the past but an integral part of the music’s development. So Family Band doesn’t recreate the work of Ornette Coleman and others, but shares its powerful and freewheeling momentum – moments of fierce intensity, introspection and the blues all combining into an emotionally complex and often cathartic whole.

Best known as a long-time lead vocalist with Incognito, Haynes brings serious soul credentials to the stage. Her career includes work with Van Morrison, Chaka Khan, Billy Ocean, Lulu, Anastacia, Leon Ware, Mario Biondi and Dave Stewart, alongside more than 14 years touring internationally with one of Britain’s most respected jazz-funk bands. events.description: NINE BELOW ZERO - 'Don't Point Your Finger' 45th Anniversary album Tour Nine Below Zero formed in late 1979 from the ashes of Stan's Blues Band. An electrifying live group, the band chose to release their debut album 'Live at the Marquee' (A&M Records, 1980) to showcase the band's considerable talent. 'Live at the Marquee' featured mainly covers of Blues classics from artists such as Otis Rush, Muddy Waters, & Freddie King along with some Nine Below Zero originals. Over the years it has become widely acknowledged as one of the finest live albums ever recorded. Nine Below Zero are one of the UK's finest Rhythm 'n' Blues groups. Named after the famous Sonny Boy Williamson song, Nine Below Zero have shared the stage with The Kinks, The Who, Chuck Berry, Eric Clapton, Squeeze, From The Jam and many more. Soul Sessions: The Neo Soul is a live music night spotlighting the very best of neo soul - curated and hosted by Soul Sessions. Neo soul emerged in the late ’90s as a modern evolution of classic soul, blending rich musicianship with elements of jazz, R&B, funk and hip-hop. Known for its honest storytelling, warm grooves and expressive vocals, the genre champions authenticity, emotional depth and artistic freedom. Set in the intimate surroundings of Soul Mama, this evening celebrates that spirit through powerful live performances and a carefully curated atmosphere rooted in culture, creativity and connection. Expect smooth rhythms, soulful melodies and performances that feel both timeless and contemporary. Whether you’re a long-time neo soul lover or discovering the sound for the first time, this is a night designed to be felt as much as heard. Good vibes, great music and soulful energy all night long. Inspiration for the night... The Soul Mama Menu offers a delightful blend of African, Caribbean, and South American cuisine. Soul Mama was listed in the “top restaurants to look forward to in 2024 list” by the Evening Standard. Please take a moment to explore our menu…

This year’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner stars two 2025 Oscar nominees - Renate Reinsve (Sentimental Value) and Sebastian Stan (The Apprentice) - in a gripping, morally complex drama that will leave you thinking about it long after the credits roll. A Romanian-Norwegian family moves to a small village at the end of a beautiful fjord. They quickly befriend their neighbours and their children settle into school. But when bruises are discovered on their daughter, rumours begin to spread. Is something wrong at home, or are they simply raising their children differently from everyone else? Winning his second Palme d’Or after 2007’s 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, Romanian director Cristian Mungiu turns a seemingly peaceful village into the setting for a tense, unsettling moral drama that refuses easy answers. Sebastian Stan gives an impressively restrained performance as the father, while Renate Reinsve is a calm, disquieting presence as his Norwegian wife. Slowly and surely, Fjord transforms an everyday community dispute into something far more disturbing.

ai.en: Lily Lyons plays Vortex Jazz Club as part of the EFG London Jazz Festival Dalston Song Club. Doors open at 6:45 pm, and music starts at 7:15 pm.

events.description: Doors 6:45 PM, Music 7:15 PM - 1 set of music About: Our monthly series brings together some of the most prominent voices in contemporary songwriting, hosted by Matthew Herd. The incredible Lily Lyons joins us this month for a London Jazz Festival special. Lily Lyons Raised between London and Somerset, Lily Lyons blends tender folk influences with emotionally incisive songwriting, creating songs that feel both intimate and quietly defiant. Inspired by artists such as Joni Mitchell, Nick Drake and Big Thief, Lily writes with a rare balance of softness and strength. Her work is rooted in honesty and human connection, embracing contradiction: joy alongside grief, tenderness alongside anger, stillness alongside emotional intensity. With a captivating live presence and a deeply personal approach to storytelling, Lily creates music that invites listeners into a world that is raw, healing, and unmistakably her own. Her debut album, “Re-Open the World” was released in 2025 to universal acclaim, and was closely followed by a live album recorded last November at St Matthias Church in Dalston. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/lilylyonsmusic/

The BBC Singers, conducted by Krista Audere, perform Parry’s Songs of Farewell, his profoundly moving cycle of wartime laments for a lost age. Confronted by both the devastation of the First World War and by his own declining health, Parry poured his response into six luminous choral motets steeped in nostalgia and grief, and widely regarded as some of the most powerful music he ever wrote. The first half of the concert looks to renewal and the natural world, pairing Caroline Shaw’s Companion Planting with one of Palestrina’s earliest works, his radiant Missa Sicut lilium inter spinas.

events.description: Thirty years ago, a chance meeting at a South London party sparked one of British electronic music?s most enduring partnerships: Morcheeba. When multi-instrumentalist Ross Godfrey invited East London singer-songwriter Skye to play him a song, her quietly powerful voice sealed the deal and the rest is trip-hop history. Three decades on, Morcheeba have released 10 studio albums, sold over 10 million records, toured the world, and become synonymous with soulful calm and cinematic cool. From headlining Meltdown Festival at the invitation of Chaka Khan to soundtracking life?s highs and lows for generations of fans, their music remains a refuge in chaotic times. In 2025, they returned with their 11th studio album, Escape The Chaos, a 12-track journey of warmth, resilience and reconnection. Blending lush electronic textures with organic grooves and Skye?s unmistakable, soul-stirring vocal, the record explores love, healing and finding peace in turbulent times. events.description: Bird on the Wire present Kiss Facility. Kiss Facility is the multidisciplinary duo of Mayah Alkhateri and Salvador Navarette, who have been working across sound, image, and performance since their first encounter. Their practice is rooted in spiritual enquiry, drawing on themes of psychic perception, ritualprotection, intimacy and the afterlife as a force of future destiny. Through symbolism and real-life emotion, Kiss Facility pushes artistic boundaries whilst examining identity as a site of self-transformation. Sonically, the project sits at the margins of modern shoegaze, built on thick guitars,submerged vocal poetry, and compressed emotion. The duo adapts the genre’s familiar language and redirects it through Arabic lyricism, private mythologies, and inward worlds rarely foregrounded in alternative music. Their upcoming album, KHAZNA (meaning safe, vault, or treasury) refers to what is kept hidden. Its themes unfold through layered vocals and unexpected sound, holding vulnerable subjects such as love, liberation, and lived experience without spectacle or declaration. The album invites listening as an act of uncovering, reaching full-circle through the themes of exploration. Created by two people who live and work together in the comfort of their home, KHAZNA feels shared rather than performed. Ready to be unraveled publicly, the album arrives in March via ambient tweets, alongside the announcement of Kiss Facility’s debut European tour and an album listening session…

ai.en: The Hanging Stars play St Matthias Church to celebrate their sixth album, Just A Day. The band plays four-part harmonies and twelve-string guitars.

events.description: London’s The Hanging Stars return with their sixth album, Just A Day – a dazzling collection of four-part harmonies, shimmering twelve-string guitars and chiming songs, touching on themes of longing, new beginnings and the fragility of the everyday. Recorded at Edwyn Collin’s legendary Clashnarrow Studios in the Scottish Highlands, the album marks a bold new chapter for the band, produced by Teenage Fanclub's Gerard Love and Dexy’s Sean Read. A line-up change at the end of 2024 proved to be a galvanising moment for The Hanging Stars. “We needed to rethink things,” says guitarist Patrick Ralla. “A new leaner approach – bass, drums, guitars, four-part harmonies. Certainly worked for The Byrds, Big Star and Teenage Fanclub.” The result is a wonderfully energising record full of catchy hooks and a renewed vision. The songs are designed to take the listener away from it all… even if it's just for a little while. Central to the record’s new direction was the involvement of Gerard Love – one third of Teenage Fanclub’s celebrated songwriting trio and the artist behind Lightships. Starting from demos exchanged between Glasgow and London, Love helped the band strip things back to their essence, ever so gently guiding them toward their finest work to date. He also joined the band for a week of recording, contributing vocals, arrangement ideas and by all accounts a mean vegan curry. Just A Day is The Hanging Stars’ third album to be recorded at Clashnarrow Studios, Helmsdale located in…

ai.en: Osibisa play Boisdale, Canary Wharf. The afrobeat band's music is served with dinner, with table reservations from 6 pm and live music at 9 pm.

events.description: Table reservations from 6 pm | Live Music: 9 pm “Jimi Hendrix watched them rehearse, Stevie Wonder joined them on drums, and Fela Kuti partied with them in Lagos…” The Guardian Formed in London in 1969 by four African and three Caribbean musicians, Osibisa stand as the founding architects of Afro-rock. They were the first Black band to break The Marquee Club in 1971, earned two UK chart hits in 1976, and became one of the most influential African-heritage groups to emerge from Britain’s music scene. Their fusion of African rhythms, Caribbean grooves, funk, jazz, rock, Latin and highlife shaped the early language of what later became known as world music. Their catalogue continues to resonate across generations, with Sunshine Day, Welcome Home and Music for Gong Gong remaining staples on global stages. Osibisa’s legacy runs deep, cited by artists from Santana and Stevie Wonder to Al Green, Johnny Nash and Bob Marley. At Boisdale of Canary Wharf, the band bring their signature blend of driving percussion, soaring horns and richly textured arrangements - the sound that made them internationally recognised as the godfathers of Afro-rock. Visit our Hine Bar and Heated Garden Terrace located on the 1st floor for pre & post-show drinks! Subscribe here to Boisdale's weekly newsletter. ai.en: Saturday Soul Lunch: Kings of Soul features Nate Simpson performing a tribute to soul's greatest singers at Boisdale, Canary Wharf. Table reservations start at noon, and live music runs from 1 to 3 pm.

events.description: Table reservations from 12pm | Live Music: 1-3pm West End vocalist Nate Simpson takes centre stage for Celebrating the Kings of Soul, a musically charged homage to the voices that shaped American R&B and soul across five defining decades. A seasoned performer with principal credits in Get Up, Stand Up! The Bob Marley Musical, Motown the Musical, The Lion King and The Crooners, Simpson has built a reputation for tonal precision, commanding phrasing and a natural ease with groove-led repertoire. His stage craft has also seen him appear across national television and radio, receive support from BBC Introducing, and share stages with Beverley Knight, Jessie J and Jacob Collier. Accompanied by a finely tuned live band, he moves through the harmonic brilliance of Stevie Wonder, the velvet urgency of Marvin Gaye and the silken phrasing of Luther Vandross with musical intelligence rather than imitation. The southern intimacy of Al Green, the Motown drive of The Four Tops and Lionel Richie’s effortless melodic touch sit alongside George Benson’s jazz-inflected elegance and the brass-powered precision of Earth, Wind & Fire. Rich arrangements, tight horn lines and a rhythm section built for precision give these songs renewed weight within Boisdale’s intimate live music restaurant setting. Served alongside a three-course Saturday lunch in our second-floor dining room overlooking Cabot Square, this is soul music at its most refined: rhythmic, romantic and rooted in heritage. events.description: Kilimanjaro and Communion ONE Present Fink + Angela Autumn The City Is Coming to Erase It All is Fink’s ninth studio album, following 2024’s Beauty In Your Wake. Recorded in Zennor, Cornwall, the album was made with a strict era-specific approach. Imagining a record Michael Chapman might have made, right down to the guitar strings. Grammy-winning producer Sam Okell helped guide the process: “If it didn’t exist in 1974, you’re not allowed to use it.” But this is nowstalgia, not nostalgia. “I want something new, but with the same ethos,” singer Fin Greenall explains. There’s a parallel between the restless 18-year-olds Fink once were and the autumn-aged family men they are now. Touring remains a compulsion as much as a joy, despite having played every major European city countless times. “The need to play your new material is so overwhelming that it trumps all the comforts and trinkets.” City is a product of this hunger for discovery, and idolatry of the album as a form – like we had in 1974. City’s cover mirrors its interior, the first song is the greeting, the instrumental closer the conclusion. It’s a story. It’s a record for people who, like its creators, are curious. People who happily face a little cold for music, who light a crackling fire back home, who sit with these songs until they’re ready to chase after their own blue sky.

Having started his musical career with Fela Kuti's Egypt 80 band in his teens, he then teamed up with childhood friend Fela's son Femi Kuti (back in the late eighties) to kick start the Positive Force - touring, recording and performing worldwide. Over forty years later, he remains a tireless ambassador for the unique musical movement all over the world. His blend of complex funk grooves, traditional Nigerian music, African percussion and an underlying sense of jazz combines with his virtuoso keyboard skills and rhythmic singing to make him one of the most respected Afrobeat authorities of his era. Hackney-born and UK-based Dele has performed all over the planet, from the Montreux Jazz Festival to Mawazine Festival in Rabat Morrocco; Ollin Khan in Mexico, South Korea and the Copenhagen Jazz Festival. Boney M sold over 100 million records during their imperial run, with "Rivers of Babylon/Brown Girl in the Ring" and "Mary’s Boy Child" both becoming UK million-selling No. 1 singles. Their album Nightflight to Venus also topped the UK Albums Chart, placing them among the defining pop-disco acts of the late 1970s. The project takes its name from Italian painter Giovanni Bragolin, famed for his “Crying Boy” paintings. The debut album I Saw Nothing Good So I Left (2018) featured the track Into Those Woods, which is now a modern-day dance floor classic. The song surpassed 10 million all-time streams in 2025, establishing BRAGOLIN as a consistent presence within the global Dark Wave and Gothic scene. In 2019, van der Velde collaborated with fellow Dutch artist ADAM TRISTAR on the second album Let Out The Noise Inside, which leaned further into electronic and synth-based production. In 2026, BRAGOLIN release their new album I Don’t Like What It Does To Me, unfolding in gradually revealed chapters. Building on the project’s signature sound, the record combines Bass VI melodies, organ lines, and rich atmospheric production. Field recordings, synthetic ocean textures, water-phones, and experimental sound sources create a layered, immersive listening experience. ai.en: Dmitry Spirin plays the Tarakany. 35 Years Tour at New Cross Inn. The band Tarakany. would have turned 35 in 2026 but stopped existing in April 2022.

events.description: Dmitry Spirin - "Tarakany! - 35 Years" TourIn 2026, the band "Tarakany!" would have marked its 35th anniversary, yet it ceased to exist in April 2022.The band's dissolution did not lead to obscurity; on the contrary, its work gained even greater relevance during the war. Global streaming statistics—including in Russia, where some songs were censored—along with YouTube views of videos and interviews (both old and new) featuring Dmitry Spirin, indicate that interest in the band's work has not waned but continues to grow, and that their songs resonate perfectly with the times we live in.Consequently, in 2026, Dmitry Spirin will embark on the "Tarakany! - 35 Years" tour.The program planned for the anniversary tour will feature all of Tarakany!'s greatest hits. Songs from last year's repertoire—such as "Ya smotryu na nikh," "Tishina — eto smert," "Vlasteliny vselennoy," and "Samyy schastlivyy chelovek na Zemle"—will be joined by hits like "5 slov," "Meshki s kostyami," "To chto ne ubivayet tebya," "Dva po sto," and others. Tarakany! anniversary concerts are always characterized by overwhelming energy, a sense of unity between the audience and the artists, and packed venues. And 2026 offers another chance to return—if only for a few hours—to the happy, old days from before the war. Yet, naturally, there will be no discussion of the war nor any performance of prophetic songs.

ai.en: KEG plays Moth Club on the Relaxing Near The Hospital album tour. The band has been experimenting with its sound since it formed six years ago.

events.description: Relaxing Near The Hospital Album Tour Keg have been experimenting with their sound ever since their conception. Over the 6 years as a band they have garnered attention for their frenetic live performances and unwavering commitment to not settling on one sound. Their new album ‘Relaxing Near the Hospital’ only further cements this ideology. At once tender and vitriolic the album is full of contradiction, each song taking a sojourn into their myriad of influences. From hefty chunks of hardcore, to Steely Dan leaning croonerish tracks the album is reminiscent of Ween in its commitment to an noncommittal sound. What feels new is a level of vulnerability which has often been hinted at in previous releases, but here feels fully established. The band have released two critically acclaimed EPs ‘Assembly’ (2021) and ‘Girders’ (2022), garnering attention from Loud and Quiet, NME, Dork, So Young and support from BBC radio 6 and Radio X. DIY are real champions of the band, awarding them a slot in their prestigious Class of 2023. Their debut album ‘Fun’s Over’ charted in the top 75 in the overall album charts, 10 in Record store charts and in the top 25 in Independent Album charts, received several 4/5 and 8/10 reviews including “Marks the beginnings of a group aiming for the big leagues” – Sound of Violence ★★★★ It is the live arena, where KEG is understood best, they’ve earnt their stripes at Greenman (Big Top), Latitude (Sunrise Arena), Sur Le Sac (CH), Sacred Ground (DE), End of The…

Their long-standing musical partnership centres on a shared love of space, clarity, and expressive storytelling, creating performances that are immersive, spontaneous, and deeply connected. Parliamentary Jazz Award-winning vocalist Emilia Märtensson is recognised as one of the most distinctive voices in UK jazz, celebrated for her expressive tone and emotionally nuanced storytelling. The Observer described her as "the new face of British jazz," while Jazzwise praised her as "a voice of quite remarkable expressive depth." Pianist, composer, and producer Matt Robinson, known for his work with Snowpoet, is acclaimed for his melodic improvisations, harmonic richness, and imaginative use of piano, synthesisers, and live electronics. Drawing inspiration from iconic European jazz duos such as Sidsel Endresen & Bugge Wesseltoft and Norma Winstone & John Taylor, Märtensson and Robinson subtly reimagine the voice-piano format through improvisation, extended techniques, and understated electronics, while preserving its essential intimacy. ai.en: Reiss Ellis Beckles plays Blues and The Abstract Truth at Vortex Jazz Club as part of the EFG London Jazz Festival. Doors open at 7:45 pm, and music starts at 8:30 pm.

events.description: Doors 7:45 PM, Music 8:30 PM - 2 sets of music Line-up: Joseph Oti - Trumpet Reiss Ellis Beckles - Alto Saxophone Houston Patton - Tenor Saxophone Phil Knights - Baritone Saxophone Simon Purcell - Piano Tom Riviere - Double Bass Laura Klain - Drum Kit About: For one night only, saxophonist and bandleader Reiss Ellis Beckles presents a live performance of Oliver Nelson’s iconic The Blues and the Abstract Truth. Featuring Nelson’s original arrangements, the ensemble brings this landmark 1961 recording to life in its entirety — celebrating its powerful melodies, sophisticated harmonies and timeless blues language. A rare opportunity to experience one of jazz’s most influential albums performed live, as originally conceived.

ai.en: The RnB Collective, a tribute to the golden era of R&B, plays Boisdale, Canary Wharf. Table reservations start at 6 pm and live music at 8:30 pm.

events.description: Table reservations from 6pm | Live Music: 8.30pm “A phenomenal tribute to the golden era of R&B. An outstanding show.” - Steve Hallum, Jump Events Back by popular demand There is a very specific kind of R&B that still owns a room: the bassline is deep, the harmonies are clean and the chorus arrives like everyone has been waiting for it. The RnB Collective brings that feeling back to Boisdale with a live set built around the 90s and 00s records people still know by heart. This is the era of slow jams, silk-smooth hooks and songs that moved between bedroom soul and dancefloor confidence without missing a step. Expect classics inspired by TLC, Usher, Blackstreet, Donell Jones and Ne-Yo, reworked with polished vocals, tight groove, rich harmonies and soulful solos. With musicians connected to the acclaimed RnB Orchestra, the show has the weight of players who understand the material from the inside: how to let a slow jam breathe, when to sit back in the pocket and when to bring the room up. It is nostalgia, yes, but not museum-piece nostalgia. These songs still move. Set in Boisdale’s intimate live music room, The RnB Collective is made for groups, celebrations, date nights and anyone who wants R&B with proper musicianship behind it. Expect the hooks, the harmonies and that dangerous moment when one person starts singing and the whole room follows. Visit our Hine Bar and Heated Garden Terrace located on the 1st floor for pre-show drinks! *Subject to availability Subscribe here…

events.description: Live Nation Presents MEEK Plus Special Guest Tom A. Smith In early autumn 2025, MEEK gave a digital stream of her anthemic signature tune, Fabulous, to a friend. He was DJing that evening in the packed, neon-hued Chinatown gay joint, Ku-Bar, London’s favoured home of emerging pop smashes. Meek is the deeply, blissfully, gloriously ironic and real surname of singer/songwriter/unapologetically outlandish pop vamp, Georgia Meek. For her forthcoming debut album, MEEK allowed herself one unwritten maxim to apply to all tunes. “These are songs that say I’m going to make my own space. I’m here, I’m fucking weird, I don’t care, deal with it.” Let’s let her take up the tale. The experience at Ku-Bar was expedient and immediately readable. “I jumped up on the bar and started lip-syncing along,” she says. “I did half of the first intro and then everyone – literally everyone in the bar - was screaming, ‘I’m so fucking fabulous.’” Fabulous is one of those tunes that lodges in the brain not just on first listen, but during the first four bars. Propulsive, energised pop majesty. “The whole place went fucking nuts, it was so fun.” In terms of road-testing your material, there can be no more stringent acid test than trying it out, loud in a neighbourhood gay disco, while high-kicking on the bar. “I knew the song was instant,” she adds. “I just didn’t know how instant.” How did MEEK get here? Like everyone that wants to shout to be heard, Meek comes from a mixture of an ordinariness she had…

ai.en: Shearwater, Loma and Any Kind play The Garage on the tour When can I see you. Shearwater and Loma both feature songwriter Jonathan Meiburg.

events.description: Shearwater + Loma + Any Kind Present 'When can I see you?' Loma and Shearwater almost seem fated to tour together. Both feature songwriter Jonathan Meiburg and engineer/producer Dan Duszynski; both have their roots in Austin, Texas; both arereleased by Seattle’s Sub Pop records. And both have a third member named Emily (Emily Lee in Shearwater, Emily Cross in Loma). But they’re different in the profound ways that only siblings can be. Cross’s calm and enveloping voice is the heart of Loma, whose pastoral, mesmerizing 2018 debut was miles away from Shearwater’s extroverted Jet Plane and Oxbow, released the previous year. Since then, each group has produced two more albums: Loma followed their self-titled first album with Don’t Shy Away (2020) and How Will I Live Without A Body? (2023), while Shearwater releasedThe Great Awakening (2022) and this year’s The New World (2026). Neither group, however, has played live since 2018v— which Meiburg insists was an accident. "Thepandemic scrambled everything," he says, "and members of both groups left the country. Suddenly putting together a tour felt almost impossible, and it took a while to come back from that.” Please be aware that each ticket purchased includes a £1 levy. This levy supports the continued improvement and sustainability of our venue, ensuring we can bring you the best possible experience at every event. We appreciate your understanding and support.

ai.en: Bruno Heinen's The Ligeti Project plays Vortex Jazz Club as part of the EFG London Jazz Festival. Doors open at 7:45 pm, and music starts at 8:30 pm.

events.description: Doors 7:45 PM, Music 8:30 PM - 2 sets of music Line-up: Bruno Heinen - Piano Heidi Vogel - Voice Alex Hitchcock - Tenor saxophone Or Bareket - Bass Gene Calderazzo - Drums Salim Akki - Percussion About: Marking the 20th anniversary of avant-garde master György Ligeti’s passing, pianist Bruno Heinen—described by The Guardian as “eclectic, eccentric, and unobtrusively erudite”—brings a thrilling rhythmic experiment to The Vortex Jazz Club. Drawing from Ligeti’s masterpiece "Musica Ricercata," the ensemble fuses the composer's eerie, iconic soundscapes—made famous by filmmaker Stanley Kubrick—with jazz exploration. Starting from minimal melodic ideas, the music expands into deep, shifting grooves. Featuring a stellar lineup of Heidi Vogel (vocals), Alex Hitchcock (saxophone), NYC-bassist Or Bareket, and an explosive two-drummer concept led by Gene Calderazzo alongside Moroccan roots/groove percussionist Salim Akki, this performance promises an unparalleled evening of spontaneous creation, celebrating Ligeti’s enduring genius.
